message.content: {"caption":"Side-by-side schematic comparing a traditional LLM-agent memory system with an agentic memory system.","description":"Two diagrams compare memory arrangements for LLM agents. In both, a globe labeled “Environment” connects to a robot icon labeled “LLM Agents” through two opposing arrows labeled “Interaction.” In the left diagram, the agent connects to a separate stack of three purple memory blocks labeled “Memory”: a right-pointing arrow labeled “Write” leads from the agent to the blocks, and a left-pointing arrow labeled “Read” leads back to the agent. In the right diagram, the agent similarly has a right-pointing “Write” arrow and a left-pointing “Read” arrow to a blue agent-like icon, with the icon and three purple memory blocks grouped in a pale-blue region labeled “Agentic Memory.” Three pairs of opposing, unlabeled arrows connect that icon to the memory blocks, indicating links in both directions. The right-hand design depicts more direct, bidirectional connections among the agentic-memory component and its stored memories than the separate store in the traditional design.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
